parts.text:
Research has been carried out into the use of a monoclonal antibody, known as VRC01, for
the prevention of HIV infection in people who are at high risk of infection.
• VRC01 was infused (injected) into volunteers once every eight weeks for 80 weeks.
• If a volunteer became infected, the strain of HIV was identified.
• For each of the different strains of HIV identified, scientists tested the effectiveness of
VRC01 to prevent HIV infection of cells grown in culture.
The results showed that the effectiveness of VRC01 varied depending on the strain of HIV.
VRC01 binds to one part of a viral glycoprotein, gp120, which is located in the HIV envelope.
HIV attaches to host cells using gp120.

parts.text:

protect a person from HIV infection.

parts.label: (iii)
parts.text:

be more successful in preventing HIV infection than using only VRC01.
